name: Grid
description: Arranges items into responsive columns with one shared gap.

columns.description: Column tracks: a count (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 12) for that many equal minmax(0, 1fr) tracks, or "auto" to fit as many minChildWidth tracks as the width allows. With minChildWidth a count becomes a ceiling that drops tracks as the grid narrows.

minChildWidth.description: Narrowest a track may get, as a CSS length. Defaults to the grid-cell measure for columns="auto"; with a count it turns the count into a ceiling. Measured against the grid's own width, never the viewport.

gap.description: Space between tracks on the layout gap scale: 0, 4, 8, 12, 16, 24

alignItems.description: Vertical alignment of items within their cells

justifyItems.description: Horizontal alignment of items within their cells

when: Cards, tiles, or media that reflow as their container narrows
Feature mosaics: Grid.Item colSpan and rowSpan around a Card
guidelines: columns="auto" with minChildWidth adapts to the grid's own width
A count plus minChildWidth caps the tracks and drops them as the pane narrows — no viewport breakpoints
gap reads the one layout scale; the shell owns the page gutter and surfaces own their inset, so Grid has no padding
Wrap a child in Grid.Item to span columns; colSpan="full" spans the row
Keep source order equal to visual order — Grid does not reorder for screen readers
accessibility: Grid is purely visual — it does not affect reading order or semantics
Ensure logical source order matches visual order for screen readers

examples.name: Default
examples.code:
import { Card } from '@/components/Card';
import { Grid } from '@/components/Grid';

<Grid columns={3} gap="md">
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Card>Two</Card>
  <Card>Three</Card>
</Grid>

examples.name: Capped Columns
examples.description: Up to three tracks, never thinner than 14rem; tracks drop as the grid narrows.
examples.code:
import { Card } from '@/components/Card';
import { Grid } from '@/components/Grid';

<Grid columns={3} minChildWidth="14rem" gap="md">
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Card>Two</Card>
  <Card>Three</Card>
</Grid>

examples.name: Auto-fill
examples.description: As many tracks as fit at the minimum width.
examples.code:
import { Card } from '@/components/Card';
import { Grid } from '@/components/Grid';

<Grid columns="auto" minChildWidth="12rem" gap="md">
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Card>Two</Card>
  <Card>Three</Card>
  <Card>Four</Card>
</Grid>

examples.name: With Spanning
examples.description: Grid.Item spans columns; colSpan="full" spans the row.
examples.code:
import { Card } from '@/components/Card';
import { Grid } from '@/components/Grid';

<Grid columns={4} gap="md">
  <Grid.Item colSpan={2}>
    <Card>Spans two</Card>
  </Grid.Item>
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Card>One</Card>
  <Grid.Item colSpan="full">
    <Card>Full width</Card>
  </Grid.Item>
</Grid>

examples.name: Form Layout
examples.description: Two fields side by side, folding to one column below 14rem each.
examples.code:
import { Field } from '@/components/Field';
import { Grid } from '@/components/Grid';
import { Input } from '@/components/Input';

<Grid columns={2} minChildWidth="14rem" gap="md">
  <Field>
    <Field.Label>First name</Field.Label>
    <Input placeholder="Ada" />
  </Field>
  <Field>
    <Field.Label>Last name</Field.Label>
    <Input placeholder="Lovelace" />
  </Field>
  <Grid.Item colSpan="full">
    <Field>
      <Field.Label>Email address</Field.Label>
      <Input type="email" placeholder="ada@example.com" />
    </Field>
  </Grid.Item>
</Grid>

relations.note: Grid commonly contains Card components for dashboard and tile layouts

propsSummary: minChildWidth: string — narrowest track; turns a count into a ceiling
Pass-through DOM props supported on Grid and Grid.Item roots (id, role, aria-*, data-*, handlers)
